candidates.name: Armyansk-Dzhankoi Gas Pipeline
candidates.researcher_notes: A UNIAN report of 15 September 2011 says the company Zangas-NGS finished the linear part of the Armyansk-Dzhankoi high-pressure trunk line. Length is 72.5 km. Zangas-NGS was the turnkey general contractor for Ukrtransgaz. The report says the line will carry up to 4.5 bcm a year of extra gas to Crimea and the owner planned to hand it over by the end of 2011. A Neftegaz.ru analysis of 12 February 2015 says the line, diameter 1000 mm, passed in 2014 to Chornomornaftogaz, which now runs it, and that it is less than 10 years old, so it was operating then. No GEM row has an Armyansk or Dzhankoi end, so this is not a match to an existing row. Crimea counts as Ukraine under the naming conventions. Chornomornaftogaz is an occupying-power operator since 2014 and is noted as such, not recorded as the Ukrainian operator. The exact commissioning date was not found. Start year is left blank. Current operating status after 2022 was not checked in a recent source, so the tier is medium. The Crimea-region fields (StartState/Province) are left blank. The 4.5 bcm/y is the added capacity stated in the 2011 report, not a confirmed design rating. The 700 million hryvnia cost is for the total project (2003 contract) and is not staged. No route found; route not mapped. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 7 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s) -> no.

candidates.name: Dzhankoi-Feodosia-Kerch Gas Pipeline
candidates.monitor_reason: length: no page states the pipeline's own length. Only a lower bound of 247 km (the Kerch Strait line was to join it at its km 247) and an unverified 268.3 km figure that no fetched page confirms. The 500 km figure on the Chernomorneftegaz page is the added length of the Armyansk-Dzhankoi trunk, the Dzhankoi-Feodosia-Kerch trunk and branch lines together, not this pipe. Sponsor and endpoints are clear.
candidates.researcher_notes: Not in the GEM roster: none of the 47 Ukraine gas rows has a Dzhankoi, Feodosia, Kerch or Crimea end. It is a different pipe from the 2016 Kuban-Crimea line (krasnodar-krai-crimea), which crosses the Kerch Strait and was staged as a new row in the Russia run. The 2014 Black Sea Oil and Gas (Chernomorneftegaz) plan says the new strait line would tie into this older trunk at its km 247. What is confirmed: the trunk is a Crimean main line with 500 mm diameter (neftegaz.ru analysis of the Chernomorneftegaz system, 2015), put into operation in 1999 according to the Naftogaz of Ukraine history page. A neftegaz.ru news item from May 2014 says it was built in 2000, and a Ukrainian Cabinet order of 17 November 2001 (no. 519-r) named a state commission to accept the finished pipeline, so the start year is 1999 to 2001 depending on source; 1999 staged as the operator's own history. It was run by Ukrtransgaz (Kharkivtransgaz, Kherson pipeline operating unit) until March 2014 and then taken over by Chernomorneftegaz under Russian-installed administration; that operator is the occupying-power builder/operator, not a Ukrainian operator, so Owner left blank pending the ownership team. Territory: wholly inside occupied Crimea, so a Ukraine row. Status operating: the 2016 tie-ins and the 2023 reports of Crimean grid use say it is in service. Length is the only missing leg of the add-threshold. To close it, find a Ukrtransgaz or Chernomorneftegaz document, or the 2001 Cabinet order text, that states the length. If a source gives 268.3 km it clears the 25 km rule and the row can be added. Route not researched. Confidence medium. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 2 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s) -> no.

candidates.name: Odeske-Holytsynske Subsea Gas Pipeline
candidates.monitor_reason: scope: field-to-field offshore line (gathering/infield), not a transmission pipeline. Sponsor, endpoints, length (83 km) and a concrete step (built, welded 20 Nov 2012) all pass, so a ruling on offshore interfield lines would move it to new_row.
candidates.researcher_notes: A Ukrinform story carried by Black Sea News says Chornomornaftogaz welded the final joint of an 83 km undersea gas pipeline on 20 November 2012. It links platform BK-1 of the Odeske gas field to platform MSP-4 of the Holytsynske gas condensate field. After commissioning, Odeske gas flows through it into the existing offshore pipeline and then to the onshore gas system of Crimea. A July 2012 Ukrainska Pravda news item reports the contract signed on 7 July 2012 with a planned length of 76 km; the 83 km figure is the as-built length. Both pages load and state the values, but they come from one company press service, so this is one source in effect. No existing row matches: the existing Ukraine roster has no offshore Black Sea line. Held as monitor because this is a short interfield link between two platforms, closer to field gathering than to transmission. Not staged as a row. If Baird rules that offshore interfield lines are in scope, the row would be Status operating, Fuel gas, Owner Chornomornaftogaz, Length 83 km, start Odeske BK-1 platform, end Holytsynske MSP-4 platform, Black Sea, in occupied Crimean waters which count as Ukraine under the naming conventions. Capacity, diameter and route were not researched. Chornomornaftogaz has been under Russian-installed control since 2014, so it would be noted as the builder in notes, not as the Ukrainian operator.
